methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Children’s National and Virginia Tech deepen pediatric AI collaboration to accelerate innovation for children - Children's National Hospital
signals.signal_reading: A high-profile pediatric AI collaboration between Children's National (DC-adjacent) and Virginia Tech creates a research hub but signals deep, specialized capability concentrated in institutional partnerships rather than distributed workforce capacity across Virginia's healthcare system.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free community AI workshops led by a Norfolk native directly target distributed skill-building and technology gap closure, representing grassroots peer learning infrastructure that could enable broad fluency beyond metro concentration zones.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA explicitly aims to democratize AI education beyond university walls into community impact, signaling intentional distribution mechanisms that could prevent Richmond from becoming an ivory tower pocket of excellence.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches online workforce training program - WDBJ7
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's online workforce training partnership with ed2go provides platform-delivered, on-demand learning to a traditionally underserved region, enabling shallow but broad adoption without requiring deep local AI expertise to develop or maintain.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Opinion piece explicitly naming AI data centers as drivers of Virginia's urban-rural divide signals infrastructure concentration without corresponding capability distribution—physical AI infrastructure doesn't equal workforce readiness or shared prosperity.
